key_evidence_spans: A 36-year-old Asian man presented with a 4-month history of worsening headaches and complete right homonymous hemianopia
Noncontrast head CT showed a left occipital intraparenchymal hemorrhage
Contrast-enhanced brain MRI revealed a left tentorial extra-axial enhancing mass with adjacent parenchymal hemorrhage, suggesting a cavernous angioma
Histopathological examination demonstrated spindle cells forming masses with branching ectatic vasculature, focal collagenous regions, and up to 20 mitoses per ten high-power fields
Immunohistochemical studies showed strong immunoreactivity for CD31, CD99, and Fli-1, with scattered S100-positive cells
The patient underwent a left occipital craniotomy; intraoperatively, the mass was found to invade the falx cerebri and adjacent cortex, limiting resection to subtotal removal
